findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink in the kitchen. Education was conducted with staff regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are using a paper towel to turn off the faucet to prevent contamination of clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw pork brats to be stored above ready-to-eat pepperoni and raw fish in the walk-in cooler. Education was conducted regarding proper storage order, and the items were rearranged. Ensure proper storage order guidelines are followed to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple small bowls and dishes to be stored below the pass-through service counter to be contaminated with splash debris and crumbs. Inspector advised staff to invert the dishes to prevent contamination of the food-contact surface. Ensure these dishes are properly stored to prevent cross-contamination prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler being stored above ready-to-eat produce. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the eggs were moved below the RTE foods. Ensure that storage order is followed with ready-to-eat foods stored above raw animal proteins, and proteins with the highest final cooking temperatures stored bottom to top.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple Time/Temperature Control for Safety Foods (TCS) being cold held at temperatures above 41°F (5°C):
(a) barbecue sauce labeled “refrigerate after opening”, probed at 61°F,
(b) blue cheese dressing labeled “refrigerate after opening”, probed at 52 °F, and
(c) chicken in batter, probed at 57 °F.
For the sauce station (a and b), inspectors checked the original containers of the manufactured products to see if items needed to be refrigerated after opening, and all but the Frank’s Red Hot Buffalo sauce needed to be refrigerated after opening. The current cold holding method was found to be insufficient, and the PIC was educated on better cold holding methods (deeper ice baths) or using time as a control (discard sauces after 4 hours if not held at 41°F or below). CORRECTED: PIC discarded the sauces.
CORRECTED: The chicken batter (c) was voluntarily discarded, and a new ice bath with ice surrounding multiple sides of the holding container was created.
Ensure that TCS foods are held at temperatures below 41°F or above 135°F. If cold holding temperatures cannot be maintained, then items should be discarded after 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that spray bottles with repackaged cleaning chemicals were not labeled. CORRECTED: PIC was informed that repackaged chemicals should be clearly and individually labeled with common names, and PIC placed corresponding labels on all spray bottles without labels. Ensure that working containers used for storing chemicals are clearly identified with common names to prevent accidental contamination or misuse.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that establishment’s test strips were expired. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and acquired new test strips during the inspetion. Ensure that sanitizing solutions used for food contact surfaces have a test kit or test strips to verify concentration of sanitizing agents.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the double door cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was between 50-60F and the following internal temperatures were recorded: parmesan cheese 54F, mozzarella cheese 51F, caesar dressing 53F, cut tomatoes 49F, and cream cheese 47F. The temperature control for safety (TCS) foods inside the temperature danger zone were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. There were several TCS foods recently brought to the double cooler from the walk-in cooler that had internal temperatures below 41F and these foods were immediately moved back into the walk-in cooler. All non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC was instructed that they cannot store TCS foods inside the cooler until it is cold holding foods at 41F or less. The inspector suggests getting immediate service for the double cooler. The inspector will return on 7/14/2025 to check on the temperature of the double cooler.

When the action was observed the inspector immediately educated the employees. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the cheese sauce was not being hot held at 135F or above. The cheese sauce had an internal temperature of 100F. The outside of the cheese sauce can stated that it ‘must be refrigerated after opening to maintain safety’. The inspector contacted CK to confirm that the cheese sauce must be hold held. The sauce must be held at 135F or above to keep the food out of the temperature danger zone (41F-135F). An employee mentioned that recently another employee had turned down the dial due to the cheese sauce being too hot. The dial of the warmer was turned up during the inspection. Before the inspector left the internal temperature of the cheese sauce was observed to be at 125F and still rising. Ensure that the temperature of the cheese sauce is checked on a regular basis to maintain food safety.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the dish machine at the bar was testing at 0 ppm (Cl). It appears that the line running into the sanitizer bucket is not carrying any sanitizer into the dish machine. The PIC and the employee working the bar were instructed to use the triple sink to sanitize. The dish machine can still be used for the wash and rinse cycle, but they must be sanitized in the triple sink. Dishes from the bar can alternatively be cleaned in the dish machine in the kitchen. Ensure that the bar dish machine is not used to sanitize until it is testing at least 100 ppm (Cl). The PIC called for service during the inspection. There will be a follow-up on 09/09/2024 to ensure that dish machine is functioning. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed various foods being held in an ice bath by the cook line. Foods being held in the ice bath includes, but is not limited too, cut tomatoes, lettuce, pickles, jalapeño, cheese, cooked bacon bites, green onions, and a corn dip with a sour cream base. The PIC stated that most of the food had been left out since the morning. The tomatoes were probed to be 55F, the lettuce 67F, and the dip 51F. The PIC stated that they were getting ready to switch the vegetables, so they voluntarily discarded the cut tomatoes and lettuce. The dip had been sitting out for under 4 hours (they go through the dip very quickly), so the inspector instructed the PIC to discarded the dip after 4 hours. The rest of the foods sitting in the ice bath were non-TCS foods meaning they were allowed to remain. The new cut tomatoes and lettuce which were brought out to replace the ones discarded were placed deeper in the ice bath so that the ice was on the bottom and all four sides of the container. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F of less at all times. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The bar dishwasher had a concentration of 0 ppm (cl) after multiple runs.  During troubleshooting, it was discovered the sanitizer had lost potency preventing the dishes to be properly sanitized which was corrected on-site.  Ensure the dishwasher is tested regularly to ensure it is properly sanitizing.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The coffee machine had a large accumulation of coffee residue.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure equipment is cleaned regularly to prevent residue build-up.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector entered the kitchen and immediately observed an employee leaning against the prep-cooler eating a bowl of food. Employee was immediately instructed to discard the food and cease eating. A personal drink was also observed sitting directly on the cutting board portion of the pre-cooler and on the shelf under a counter near clean dishes. Personal drinks were immediately discarded. Eating within the kitchen in areas where food may become contaminated is not allowed at any time. Drinking within the kitchen near food preparation areas is not allowed at any time unless a cup with a lid and straw is used. Ensure that staff is aware of proper policies regarding eating and drinking in the kitchen and that eating in the kitchen ceases immediately. Foods were discarded and behavior was corrected during the inspection. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time. 

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee eating and drinking personal food/drink in the kitchen and did not wash hands after discarding the food. Employee returned to working with clean dishes without hand washing. Employee claims that hands were washing in the dish sink but no hand washing had occurred. Ensure that all employees understand that hand washing must be performed in a proper hand sink, using the proper procedure and at the correct frequencies to prevent contamination of foods and food-contact surfaces. A follow-up has been issued for Thursday 11/16/2023 to ensure compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code handwashing requirements. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed x5 dented cans stocked in on the can rack for service. After being stocked in, inspector must assume that the cans may be used in the production of foods served to consumers. As such, cans with dents must be discarded/separated immediately and may not be used for food service. Cans which are dented along any seams to an extent that the integrity of the can is no longer guaranteed must be returned and/or discarded and MAY NOT be used/served. A follow-up is issued for 11/21/2023 due to the upcoming holiday. Ensure that dented cans are checked and returned before being stocked in or are immediately separated away from cans used for service. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 07/18/2022.

Inspector observed mold growth along the upper-rear side of the ice machine baffle where water drops form and stay stationary. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned often enough to prevent mold growth and that staff is aware of the need to clean all areas of the ice machine frequently. 

The can opener was observed to have some dried accumulated residue on the blade. Although improved from the previous inspection, all food residue must be removed at minimum every 4-hours to prevent accumulation. Ensure that the can opened is cleaned and sanitized every 4-hours at minimum. 

Inspector will return on 11/21/2023 to ensure that all food-contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized as required. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Date marking within the walk-in cooler is excellent. Date marking within the double upright cooler in the kitchen is hit-or-miss. Several prepared items were stored in this cooler without any date marking despite being held for later service. Ensure that all prepared items held more than 24 hours are date marked as required. Inspector will return on 11/21/2023 to check date marking in the kitchen coolers at that time. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 4/8/2023.

Inspector observed that the caulking behind the triple sink is molded along the area closes to the dish machine. This area is prone to frequent molding. Ensure that the sink is re-caulked and that staff are cleaning and sanitizing these surfaces to prevent a rapid build-up of mold. The hand sink is observed to be pulled away from the wall with no caulking. The distance behind the hand sink is less than an inch and is not designed to be moved. As such, the back of the hand sink must be caulked to prevent accumulation of residue, debris and water behind the sink. Ensure that caulking is completed by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 7/29/2021.

Inspector observed several personal items including a phone case and personal drinks stored above or around food service areas. Ensure that personal items are stored in designated areas away from food service, food storage, and clean dishes/utensils. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wire shelf with dust accumulation above the clean dish portion of the dish sink, the edge of a shelf soiled with dried sauce, and some buildup of food debris on the can opener. All food contact surfaces AND non-food-contact surfaces must be cleaned often enough to preclude the accumulation of debris and other residue. Operator immediately had indicated areas cleaned except the wire shelving with dust buildup. Facility has a specific individual who cleans the upper areas of the kitchen and will be contacted to clean these shelves. Ensure that food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces remain free of residue and debris. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulking behind the triple sink is observed to be deteriorating and developing black residue. Inspector discussed with operator that the intent behind requiring such surfaces to be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable is to prevent microbial growth and the accumulation of residue and debris in areas which cannot be cleaned easily such as behind the back portion of the sink itself which cannot be reached without moving the sink. Ensure that all surfaces of the facility subject to moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.comment: 4-602.11: Observed the can opener was significantly soiled from use and needed to be cleaned. Operator had the can opener run through the dish washer to remove old food.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Observed taco meat in the walk in cooler at 78F in the middle at approximately 5:30pm The meat was prepared this afternoon and placed to cool around 1:30pm. We discussed various methods of cooling focusing on shallow pans and using the freezer to knock down the temperature. The meat is being reheated to 165F on the stove top and will be placed to cool properly in shallow metal pans.

3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the taco meat to be in a plastic container that is greater than 3 inches deep with the lid tightly closed. Meat is being reheated and will be placed to cool properly. Use methods discussed including shallow pans and allowing heat to move away from the food by leaving the food loosely covered or open to the air during cooling. 

3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.comment: Observed scoop in soiled water. Ensure proper storage methods for in-use utensils occur. Reference 3-304.12 (C).
